title: Higher-Power Divisibility for Zero-Sum Coordinate Functions
summary: Saturation gives a dimension-dependent divisibility guarantee, while zero-sum functions have a baseline of divisibility by two; the open task is to find examples with a higher power-of-two divisor.

formal_statement.body: For a coordinate function $f$ of a primitive on an affine input space $X$ of dimension $d$, saturation implies that the number of inputs $x\in X$ satisfying $f(x)=1$ is divisible by $2^{d-1}$; when $f$ sums to zero, the stated baseline divisibility is only by $2$. The question is whether one can construct or identify zero-sum coordinate functions $f$ for which the number of solutions to $f(x)=1$ is divisible by a higher power of two than this baseline.

scope.domain: Structural divisibility properties of Boolean coordinate functions in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: f is a coordinate function of a primitive on an affine input space X of dimension d
f sums to zero for the target case
parameters: the power of two dividing the number of inputs satisfying f(x)=1
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct or identify zero-sum coordinate functions f for which the number of solutions to f(x)=1 is divisible by a higher power of two than the baseline divisibility by two.

progress.summary: The source presents this as a natural question after contrasting the saturation divisibility bound with the weaker zero-sum baseline, asking for zero-sum cases with a larger power-of-two divisor.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Ultrametric integral cryptanalysis
